teaser.text: Digital Realty makes money by providing the physical places where other companies run their digital businesses. Its dollar flows become clear when we follow the buildings, the customers, the leases, and the ownership behind them.

stock.title: Digital Realty stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Digital Realty's stock forecast weighs bear, base and bull cases, cash generation, dilution and today's valuation.
stock.opening: The probability-weighted price reaches $181.79 in October 2029, with the base case at 54%, the bear case at 28% and the bull case at 18%. It hinges on timely lease conversion and per-share growth.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Digital Realty's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Digital Realty's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast puts Digital Realty near today’s price after one year, then modestly higher. The probability-weighted price is $170.78 in October 2027, roughly flat including dividends. It rises to $177.76 in October 2028, a 7% total return. By October 2029, it reaches $181.79, a 12% total return.

The range is much wider than the weighted result suggests. In October 2029, the bear case gives $91.32, while the bull case gives $306.63. The bear, base and bull probabilities are 28%, 54% and 18%, respectively.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Digital Realty's forecast?

paragraphs.text: The evidence supports faster growth but also explains the restraint. Same-capital cash NOI grew 7.2%, cash renewal rents rose 25.4%, and 63% of the construction pipeline was pre-leased. However, the average signing-to-commencement lag was nine months, while development capex and dividends exceeded operating cash in the first half of 2026. The bear case therefore gives AFFO of $2,750 million, $2,820 million and $2,900 million; the bull gives $3,200 million, $3,600 million and $4,050 million. Management’s Core FFO guidance of $8.15–$8.20 per share and planned development capex of $4,250–$4,750 million provide an operating cross-check, not AFFO guidance.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Digital Realty really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation creates a second qualification. It is not a current cash payment, so Digital Realty adds it back in AFFO. But issuing shares to employees can dilute each shareholder’s future claim on earnings. AFFO should therefore be read beside diluted share growth.

FFO per share rose about 9% while diluted shares rose about 22%; AFFO supported a 74.5% payout ratio in 2025. Leverage improved from its 2022 high.

dividend.title: Digital Realty dividend
dividend.meta_description: Digital Realty's dividend history, cash coverage, yield and key risks explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: Digital Realty pays an annual dividend of $4.88 per share, or a current quarterly dividend of $1.22. Its operating cash has repeatedly covered dividends, but development and capital spending can exceed what remains.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Digital Realty's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Digital Realty pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from $4.94 to $5.00 and then $5.08 per share. The bear remains at $4.88 throughout, while the bull reaches $4.96, $5.12 and $5.28. The current quarterly dividend is $1.22, and the annual rate stayed at $4.88 from 2022 through 2025. A 74.5% AFFO payout ratio leaves room for modest increases, but construction spending and dividends already compete with operating cash.

blocks.heading: Is Digital Realty's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The company’s operating cash has repeatedly covered dividends while falling short of development and capital spending. The remaining construction bill therefore requires property sales, joint-venture partners, debt or new shares. That is the central funding tension: growth needs capital today, while new buildings produce rent only later.

blocks.heading: What could change Digital Realty's dividend?

paragraphs.text: The evidence supports faster growth but also explains the restraint. Same-capital cash NOI grew 7.2%, cash renewal rents rose 25.4%, and 63% of the construction pipeline was pre-leased. However, the average signing-to-commencement lag was nine months, while development capex and dividends exceeded operating cash in the first half of 2026. The bear case therefore gives AFFO of $2,750 million, $2,820 million and $2,900 million; the bull gives $3,200 million, $3,600 million and $4,050 million. Management’s Core FFO guidance of $8.15–$8.20 per share and planned development capex of $4,250–$4,750 million provide an operating cross-check, not AFFO guidance.

During 2027 and 2028, prompt starts from pre-leased projects would move earnings toward the bull case. During 2028 and 2029, lower equity needs, more asset recycling and contained debt costs would improve per-share growth and support multiple expansion. Higher funding needs, rising dilution or delayed backlog conversion would produce the opposite result.

blocks.heading: What has Digital Realty guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Management’s July 23 outlook covers the year ending December 2026. Its main measure is Core FFO per share excluding net promote income. FFO adds real-estate depreciation back to GAAP profit, while Core FFO removes additional unusual items, so the measure focuses more closely on rental operations.

blocks.heading: Did Digital Realty keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Digital Realty said FFO per share and signings exceeded the maximum bonus levels in 2025, while same-store cash NOI reached its target. Power’s annual performance bonus was 185% of target. The measures are concrete, but management still chooses the targets and their weighting.

blocks.heading: What do Digital Realty's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: The latest quarter was operationally strong, but unusual gains made the headline earnings look stronger than ordinary rent growth. Revenue grew faster than NOI, which shows why the top line can overstate property improvement when acquisitions, reimbursements, and service mix change.

The earnings jump also included $187.9 million of net promote income from buying out joint-venture interests. An insurance settlement added $94 million after tax, with about $27 million treated as business-interruption recovery. Core FFO per share was $2.65 including the promote and $2.13 excluding it. The second figure is the better guide to recurring momentum, although it still includes the business-interruption recovery.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Digital Realty's next results?

paragraphs.text: Digital Realty scheduled $635 million of annualized rent to commence in the second half of 2026, with 45% expected in Q3 and 55% in Q4. Annualized rent is the yearly amount implied by a lease; it is not twelve months of rent already collected. The October 29, 2026 results should show how much of that schedule became actual revenue.
